nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then $t_j = 0$ for some $j \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Engel trajectories vanish at a positive step

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then $t_i = 0$ for some $i \le a + 1$.
nodes.title: An Engel trajectory started at $a$ vanishes within $a + 1$ steps

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $a$ be natural numbers with $1 \le a \le n$. Then the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ is at most the maximal Engel length $M(n) = \max_{1 \le b \le n} L(n, b)$.
nodes.title: Each Engel length is at most the maximal Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers with $j \ge 1$, and let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then the Engel length $L(n, a)$ satisfies $L(n, a) \le j$.
nodes.title: The Engel length is at most any positive vanishing step

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ satisfies $L(n, a) \ge 1$.
nodes.title: The Engel length is positive

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $t_0 = a, t_1, t_2, \dots$ be the Engel trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. The Engel length $L(n, a)$ is the least $j \ge 1$ with $t_j = 0$.
nodes.title: Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $B$ be natural numbers. If the Engel length $L(n, a)$ of $a$ with respect to $n$ satisfies $L(n, a) \le B$ for every $a$ with $1 \le a \le n$, then the maximal Engel length $M(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} L(n, a)$ (with $M(0) = 0$) satisfies $M(n) \le B$.
nodes.title: A uniform bound on Engel lengths bounds the maximal Engel length

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, the maximal Engel length is $M(n) = \max_{1 \le a \le n} L(n, a)$, where $L(n, a)$ is the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$; for $n = 0$ the maximum is over the empty set and $M(0) = 0$.
nodes.title: Maximal Engel length

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $k$ and $u$ with $k \ne 0$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $k$ equals $u$ if and only if $u < k$ and $k$ divides $n + u$.
nodes.title: Characterization of the negated remainder

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$ with $k \ge 1$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $k$ is the unique $u$ with $0 \le u < k$ and $u \equiv -n \pmod{k}$: it equals $0$ when $k$ divides $n$ and $k - (n \bmod k)$ otherwise. For $k = 0$ it is defined to be $0$.
nodes.title: Negated remainder

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, let $L$ be the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$. Then the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is $0$ at step $L$.
nodes.title: Engel trajectory vanishes at the Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $L$ be the Engel length of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $1 \le j < L$, then the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is nonzero at step $j$.
nodes.title: Engel trajectory is nonzero at positive steps before the Engel length

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $t$ be natural numbers with $t \ne 0$. Then the Engel remainder trajectory of $t$ with respect to $n$ is, at step $1$, the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t$: the unique natural number $u < t$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t}$.
nodes.title: First step of the Engel trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j = 0$, then $t_{j+1} = 0$.
nodes.title: Zero is absorbing for the Engel trajectory

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $a$ and $j$ be natural numbers and let $t_0, t_1, \dots$ be the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$. If $t_j \ne 0$, then $t_{j+1}$ is the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$: the unique natural number $u < t_j$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t_j}$.
nodes.title: Step of the Engel trajectory at a nonzero term

nodes.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ has value $a$ at step $0$.
nodes.title: Initial term of the Engel trajectory

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $a$, the Engel remainder trajectory of $a$ with respect to $n$ is the sequence $t_0, t_1, t_2, \dots$ of natural numbers with $t_0 = a$ and, for every $j \ge 0$, $t_{j+1} = 0$ if $t_j = 0$, while if $t_j \ne 0$ then $t_{j+1}$ is the negated remainder of $n$ modulo $t_j$: the unique natural number $u < t_j$ with $u \equiv -n \pmod{t_j}$. Once the trajectory reaches $0$ it stays there.
nodes.title: Engel remainder trajectory

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
